terminology_policy.instruction: Use approved XQ style names exactly as written. Do not substitute alternative style labels.

D.name: Dominance
D.core_focus: How you tend to approach problems, challenges, authority, and results.
higher_expression: May focus strongly on results and forward movement
May be comfortable taking control when action is needed
lower_expression: May prefer cooperation over direct confrontation
May take more time before challenging existing direction
May be less motivated by competition or control
family_considerations: Differences in pace and directness can affect conflict
High directness may be experienced differently by more reserved team members
Clear expectations can reduce unnecessary power struggles

I.name: Influence
I.core_focus: How you tend to approach people, communication, persuasion, and social interaction.
higher_expression: May enjoy interaction and verbal processing
May influence through enthusiasm and persuasion
May place importance on connection and engagement
lower_expression: May prefer facts or reflection over spontaneous social interaction
May be less motivated by visibility or social recognition
family_considerations: Differences in communication volume and frequency can create misunderstandings
Expressive team members may need to leave room for quieter processing styles
Recognition and interpersonal feedback may carry different importance for different people

S.name: Steadiness
S.core_focus: How you tend to approach pace, consistency, change, patience, and support.
higher_expression: May value patience, cooperation, and stable relationships
May take time to adjust to sudden change
May provide dependable support to others
lower_expression: May prefer faster movement and greater variety
May adjust more readily to rapid change
May become restless with prolonged routine
family_considerations: Unexpected change may affect team members differently
Advance notice can reduce avoidable stress
Differences in pace should not automatically be interpreted as resistance or impatience

C.name: Compliance
C.core_focus: How you tend to approach standards, accuracy, structure, rules, and details.
higher_expression: May value accuracy and clear standards
May examine details before reaching conclusions
May prefer established processes and defined expectations
May be cautious about avoidable errors
lower_expression: May be more flexible about structure or procedure
May act with less need for detailed analysis
May prioritize speed or adaptability over precision
family_considerations: Different standards for detail can create friction
Rules and expectations should be explicit rather than assumed
A need for accuracy should not automatically be interpreted as criticism

Conductor.definition: A primarily results-focused behavioral pattern characterized by directness, decisiveness, and a tendency to move quickly toward objectives.
potential_strengths: Can create momentum when action is needed
potential_challenges: May move faster than others are ready for
May become impatient with lengthy discussion

avoid: Hiding the main issue under excessive detail
Taking directness personally without examining intent

Persuader.definition: A fast-paced, persuasive behavioral pattern combining strong results orientation with interpersonal influence.
potential_strengths: Can help move groups toward decisions
potential_challenges: May move quickly from discussion to action
May underestimate the amount of detail others need
Can become frustrated by slow progress

do: Connect ideas to action and outcomes

Promoter.definition: A people-oriented behavioral pattern characterized by communication, enthusiasm, social engagement, and interpersonal influence.
potential_strengths: Can help maintain positive interpersonal energy
potential_challenges: May rely heavily on verbal interaction

Relater.definition: A relationship-centered behavioral pattern combining interpersonal warmth with patience, support, and cooperation.
potential_challenges: May place harmony ahead of necessary disagreement

Supporter.definition: A steady and supportive behavioral pattern characterized by patience, reliability, consistency, and relational stability.
potential_strengths: May remain patient during difficult situations
potential_challenges: Can tolerate problems too long before confronting them
May need time to process major changes

Coordinator.definition: A stable and systematic behavioral pattern combining consistency with attention to standards, structure, and reliability.
potential_challenges: May be uncomfortable with sudden change
May need more information before acting
May struggle when expectations are ambiguous

Analyzer.definition: A precise and analytical behavioral pattern characterized by attention to standards, accuracy, logic, and careful evaluation.
potential_challenges: Can appear critical when focused on accuracy
May delay action while seeking more information
Can become frustrated by unclear expectations

Implementor.definition: A results-focused and systematic behavioral pattern combining decisiveness with analysis, standards, and problem-solving.
potential_strengths: May combine action with careful evaluation
